```{r}
library(brms)       # Bayesian Regression Model
library(bayesplot)  # Diagnostics
library(loo)        # LOOCV Model comparison
library(tidyverse)  # Data manipulation
library(corrplot)   # Correlation Matrix Visualization
```

# Exploratory Data Analysis

```{r}
dat <- read.csv("data.csv")
dim(dat)[1]
```

```{r}
dat$Season <- factor(dat$Season)

# select the continuous variables
num <- dat %>% 
  select(PH, IFP, NLP, NGP, NGL, NS, MHG, GY)

# check the correlation matrix
cov <- cor(num)

corrplot(cov, 
         addCoef.col = "black",
         tl.col = "red",
         number.cex = 0.7)
```

To avoid collinearity, we choose the PH, NLP as the regressors.

# Fitting

```{r}
set.seed(123)

# BRM, using Markov Chain Monte Carlo Method
fit <- brm(GY ~  Season + PH + IFP + NLP, data = dat)

# interaction model
fit.2 <- brm(GY ~ Season * (PH + IFP + NLP), data = dat)
```

# Diagnostics

```{r}
summary(fit)
```

```{r}
summary(fit.2)
```

According to the outputs, all ESS values are larger than the standard diagnostic threshold of 1000, we can safely conclude that both models are reliable.
And since all parameters have $\hat{R}=1$, it implies that the independent MCMC chains have reached a perfect consensus and successfully converged, signaling that the sampling process is stable and the results are mathematically reliable.


```{r}
# trace plots
mcmc_trace(fit, c("b_Season2", "b_PH", "b_IFP", "b_NLP"))
```

```{r}
mcmc_trace(fit.2, c("b_Season2", "b_PH", "b_IFP", "b_NLP", "b_Season2:PH", "b_Season2:IFP", "b_Season2:NLP"))
```

Both trace plots have good patterns, which perfect mixing and horizontal stationarity across all four chains. This implies that the MCMC algorithm successfully converged to a stable posterior distribution.

# Posterior Predictive Check

```{r}
# Verify that the fitted values
pp_check(fit, ndraws = 100)
```

```{r}
pp_check(fit.2, ndraws = 100)
```

The fitted values match the distribution of the original distributions, hence both models fit well.

# Model Selection

```{r}
set.seed(123)

# Using LOOCV to compare two models
loo.1 <- loo(fit)
loo.2 <- loo(fit.2)
comparison_results <- loo_compare(loo.1, loo.2)
comparison_results
```

By checking the $Ratio = \frac{|elpd\_diff|}{se\_diff}$, the ratio of fit > fit.2, which implies a better performance. Hence we should keep the interaction term.

# Inference & Visualization

```{r}
# 95% CI for the coefficients
fixef(fit.2)
```

```{r}
# posterior distributions of the coefficients
mcmc_areas(fit.2, "b_Season2", prob = 0.95)
```

```{r}
mcmc_areas(fit.2, "b_PH", prob = 0.95)
```

```{r}
mcmc_areas(fit.2, "b_IFP", prob = 0.95)
```

```{r}
mcmc_areas(fit.2, "b_NLP", prob = 0.95)
```

```{r}
mcmc_areas(fit.2, "b_Season2:PH", prob = 0.95)
```

```{r}
mcmc_areas(fit.2, "b_Season2:IFP", prob = 0.95)
```

```{r}
mcmc_areas(fit.2, "b_Season2:NLP", prob = 0.95)
```

```{r}
bayes_R2(fit.2)
```
